evidence.quote: I judge that U.S. inflation expectations today do reside at the low end of a range I consider consistent with our price‑stability mandate.
I myself believe that the range of plausible estimates of u* extends to 4 percent and below and includes the current unemployment rate of 3.6 percent.
there is no evidence that rising wages are putting excessive upward pressure on price inflation.
Persistent inflation shortfalls carry the risk that longer-term inflation expectations become anchored below the stated inflation goal.
In many models that incorporate the ELB, these makeup strategies lead to better average performance on both legs of the dual mandate.

parsed.rationale: This framework-review speech offers no near-term rate signal, but it leans dovish: inflation expectations sit at the low end of the acceptable range, there is no wage-driven inflation pressure, and the current unemployment rate may not be beyond full employment. It also emphasizes lower-bound and inflation-undershoot risks and discusses makeup strategies that would keep rates lower for longer.
